channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental Protection Agency notes that economic trees are being cut, threatening food security and increasing exposure to climate change.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents fail to reach presidency
item.description: No vice president has ever been elected president in Sierra Leone's history.

item.title: Nairobi court suspends online alcohol sales
item.description: High Court orders strict licensing and age verification for digital alcohol vendors.

item.title: National Assembly approves government policy statement
item.description: Lawmakers voted 145 to 21 to adopt the government's general policy statement presented by the prime minister.

item.title: Plaine-Magnien Star defeats Entente Boulet Rouge 4-0
item.description: Plaine-Magnien Star secured a dominant victory in their opening National D1 match on November 9, 2026.

item.title: Six candidates vie for Cape Verde presidency
item.description: One candidate claims divine calling, another faces harsh criticism.

item.title: Nigeria's FX turnover falls 51% to $1.81bn
item.description: Dollar transactions in Nigeria's foreign exchange market dropped by $1.90bn in the week ending November 6.

item.title: Togo government to spend 34.2 billion FCFA on fuel subsidies
item.description: The government will increase fuel subsidies by 20 billion FCFA to shield consumers from rising international oil prices.

item.title: Guinea closes Dar-es-Salam dump site
item.description: Conakry's waste management shifts to Baritodé, increasing transport costs and collection challenges.

item.title: Tiken Jah Fakoly fled Ivory Coast after death threats
item.description: The reggae star left Abidjan in 2002 following political unrest and criticism of leaders.

item.title: UN declares climate change a global health pandemic
item.description: Global temperatures hit 1.47 °C above pre-industrial levels, straining health systems and causing millions of deaths.

item.title: National Bank of Malawi launches electric vehicle
item.description: The K74 million vehicle is part of the bank's push for environmental, social, and governance principles.

item.title: UN to discuss Minurso mandate after Russian veto
item.description: The UN General Assembly will debate the future of the UN mission in Western Sahara following Russia's Security Council veto.

item.title: DR Congo launches digital leadership meeting
item.description: Minister Augustin Kibasa Maliba opened the second annual gathering for public sector IT and digital heads in Kinshasa.

item.title: Sánchez rules out Ceuta, Melilla talks with Morocco
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez reaffirmed support for Moroccan autonomy in the Sahara dispute.

item.title: Burkina Faso plans 21st digital week for November 2026
item.description: The event will focus on technological sovereignty, secure digital transformation, and inclusion.

item.title: Algerian election posters hide female candidates' faces
item.description: Anonymised images on campaign posters for the November 28 local elections echo a trend seen since 2012.

item.title: BAD trains Burkina Faso project managers on environmental rules
item.description: The African Development Bank is holding a five-day workshop in Ouagadougou for project staff.

item.title: Ghanaian judicial unions suspend strike
item.description: JUSAG and SSAJUG call off industrial action after government engagement on salary reviews.

item.title: Guinea sets dates for regional and senatorial election campaigns
item.description: President Mamadi Doumbouya announced campaign periods for November 29 regional and December 20 senatorial votes.

item.title: Malawi NGOs challenge deregistration
item.description: Civil society groups argue the regulator overstepped by cancelling registrations without prior warnings or corrective actions.

item.title: Eswatini MPs want chiefs stripped of stamp issuing powers
item.description: Lawmakers debated the Youth Enterprise Revolving Fund, raising concerns about underfunding and land insecurity.

item.title: Djibouti parliament discusses cybersecurity lessons
item.description: National Security Director Hassan Said Khaireh and parliament officials reviewed digital threats and best practices.

item.title: Ghana artists tap pop culture for climate action stories
item.description: Creative sector leaders and activists met at the Climate x Culture Summit 2026 to discuss integrating climate messages into art.

item.title: Niger trains energy planners with IAEA support
item.description: A two-week workshop in Niamey aims to improve national energy demand forecasting using specialized software.

item.title: Midea launches Space Master refrigerator in Nigeria
item.description: The appliance aims to solve common household challenges of limited food storage space.

item.title: Morocco raises transport fuel subsidies by 60%
item.description: Government allocates MAD 400 million more to prevent rising costs from affecting consumer prices.

item.title: Niger sets December 2026 deadline for field clearance
item.description: Tillabéri governor Maina Boukar announced the date to prevent farmer-herder conflicts and protect harvests.

item.title: Malawi court to decide bishop's bail on November 20
item.description: Prosecutors do not oppose bail for Bishop Medram Felix Chirwa in a murder case but seek strict conditions.

item.title: Bonoua forms local security committee
item.description: A new committee aims to improve safety by involving residents in prevention efforts.

item.title: Tunisia tourism faces climate, water, energy challenges
item.description: Houssem Ben Azouz of Fi2T calls for reforms to boost profitability and resilience in the sector.

item.title: Sudan closes Ethiopian consulate after drone complaint
item.description: Khartoum retaliated by expelling Ethiopian diplomats following a formal complaint to the UN Security Council.

item.title: Séquence FC takes second place in Ligue 2
item.description: The Dixinn club defeated Flamme Olympique 2-1 to climb the league standings.

item.title: Rwanda receives genocide fugitive Jean Leonard Teganya from U.S.
item.description: Teganya, a former medical student, arrived at Kigali International Airport on a chartered flight on Monday, November 9, 2026.

item.title: Old Mutual urges employers to support employee well-being
item.description: The financial services firm called for a holistic approach to worker welfare beyond salaries and productivity.

item.title: MP questions air ambulance operation since 2003
item.description: A Learjet 31 air ambulance, equipped for N$500 000, may not have flown since 2003, says Nelson Kalangula.

item.title: FG suspends broadcast licence fee reviews
item.description: The Federal Government halts all reviews of broadcast licence fees indefinitely due to rising operational costs.

item.title: Egypt renews bid for ITU Council seat
item.description: Minister Raafat Hendy seeks African representation at the Doha plenipotentiary conference.

item.title: Cairo opens first stray dog shelter
item.description: The 5,000 sq m facility in El Tebbin can house up to 700 dogs and includes operating theatres and a veterinary pharmacy.

item.title: Atiku's son joins APC campaign
item.description: Atiku junior collapsed his 'Haske' group structure into the ruling party to support President Tinubu's re-election.

item.title: Russia offers 75 scholarships to Equatorial Guinea students
item.description: Alexander Kulikov highlights university training, Russian language learning, and cultural exchange projects.

item.title: Burkina radiologists discuss medical imaging innovations
item.description: Professionals met in Ouagadougou on November 6-7, 2026, to explore technological advancements for patient care and radiation safety.

item.title: Algeria targets $7 billion non-hydrocarbon exports by 2026
item.description: The country aims to increase non-hydrocarbon exports from over $5 billion in 2025 to $7 billion by 2026.

item.title: Cameroon parliament to debate 2027 budget
item.description: Lawmakers will review spending and revenue proposals aiming for increased public investment.

item.title: Moov Africa Tchad to help 300 youths find jobs
item.description: The telecommunications company will collect CVs and select candidates for professional integration in N'Djamena.

item.title: Zambia's growth hinges on private investment, says finance minister
item.description: Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane stated that government spending alone cannot achieve development ambitions.

item.title: Morocco hosts Israeli defense delegation
item.description: Officials discuss defense cooperation, military equipment, and cybersecurity during a visit by Israeli Defense Ministry Director General Amir Baram.

item.title: Ex-soldiers share values with university students
item.description: Ouagadougou conference aimed to instill patriotism, discipline, and resilience in young people.

item.title: Spanish consulate staff invested 120 million DA in Algerian real estate
item.description: Investigators found six properties in Algiers linked to an illegal visa trafficking scheme operating for over a decade.

item.title: Lamine Goro honored for newspaper distribution
item.description: The 5th media Salon in Bamako recognized his daily work delivering Malian newspapers to readers.

item.title: Mogadishu police clash with residents over forced evictions
item.description: Three protesters killed before armed residents ambushed police in Daynile district, forcing officers to abandon wounded.

item.title: CHADEMA says police tortured detained members
item.description: The opposition party claims 10 leaders and members are held without bail or lawyers, alleging mistreatment.

item.title: Moroccan parties reject Spanish World Cup final threats
item.description: Political figures in Morocco criticized Spanish opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo's demands regarding the 2030 World Cup final.

item.title: Algeria loses two key players before Togo match
item.description: Forward Mohamed Bachir Belloumi and defender Jaouen Hadjam are out with injuries for the CAN 2027 qualifiers.

item.title: SOGEAG launches hospitality week at Conakry airport
item.description: The airport management company aims to improve passenger experience with personalized attention and cultural events.

item.title: Ethiopian women make reusable sanitary pads
item.description: Hanan Ahmed's company produces 1,000 washable pads daily to help girls stay in school.

item.title: Nine Zimbabweans arrested for alleged Russia-Ukraine war plan
item.description: Five appeared in Kempton Park and four in Johannesburg courts, facing charges under the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act.

item.title: Tanzanian College professor urges parents to teach internet laws
item.description: Professor Robert Mashenene advised parents to guide children on social media use and Artificial Intelligence for academic benefit.

item.title: Senegal wins gold in men's 3x3 basketball
item.description: The host nation's young men secured the gold medal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Koutoukagbe wins Bébédjia youth football tournament
item.description: Koutoukagbe defeated Dangdin 4-1 on penalties after a 0-0 draw in the Bébédjia youth football tournament final.

item.title: Juba County talks with six markets on administration handover
item.description: County authorities met market representatives to discuss strengthening local administration and improving market organisation.

item.title: Mali's prime minister calls for security innovation
item.description: Abdoulaye Maïga opened the Bamako International Defence and Security Exhibition 2026, focusing on modern threats.

item.title: Alger accuses France over EU statement on Niger troop deployment
item.description: The European Union's foreign affairs spokesperson addressed troop movements in Niger on October 30.

item.title: Chad election agency names six legislative candidates
item.description: The National Election Management Agency announced the provisional list for the Assoungha partial election on November 9, 2026.

item.title: South Sudan government and African Parks eye wildlife for economic growth
item.description: Officials and conservationists see potential for tourism, jobs, and investment beyond oil resources.

item.title: Ethiopian Jews mark Sigd holy day in Jerusalem
item.description: Thousands gathered in Jerusalem to mark the holy day of Sigd, a tradition of introspection and prayer.

item.title: Malawi skips Russia-Africa summit amid recruitment concerns
item.description: Activists criticize government absence from Moscow meeting, citing deceptive recruitment of youth for war.

item.title: Businessman denies receiving N$148 million loan
item.description: Benjamin Hauwanga claims he never accessed funds despite signing loan agreements for Bank Windhoek money.

item.title: Rwandan students showcase culture at Abu Dhabi festival
item.description: Students presented Rwanda's heritage and tourism at Afro Fest 2026 held at New York University Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Nuwagaba urges Uganda to fund local research
item.description: Bank of Uganda deputy governor says importing solutions weakens the economy and pressures the currency.

item.title: Angola registers over five million voters
item.description: The electoral registration process, which began on June 15, 2026, has seen more than five million eligible citizens update their details.

item.title: Zambia boxers secure third place in Kinshasa
item.description: Team Zambia won three men's titles at the IBA Africa Elite Championships with five boxers.

item.title: Matlala testifies at Madlanga Commission
item.description: Vusimuzi Matlala appeared at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry in Pretoria on November 9, 2026.

item.title: Egypt permanently lists Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist entity
item.description: A decision published in the Official Gazette on Monday, November 9, ends the possibility of the group’s listing expiring.

item.title: Tanzania horticultural exports reach 569m US dollars
item.description: The value of Tanzania's horticultural exports nearly doubled over four years, reaching 569m US dollars in 2024.

item.title: Mali aims to cut emissions by 25.22% by 2035
item.description: The nation presented its updated climate targets at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9, 2026.

item.title: UNDP launches Liberia's law reform plan
item.description: The five-year strategy aims to modernize the legal framework and improve access to justice by 2030.

item.title: Angolan bishops urge focus on citizens' needs
item.description: Catholic leaders call for transparent resource management and prioritizing family farming.

item.title: EAGB workers accuse management of harmful practices
item.description: Staff at Guinea-Bissau's electricity and water company cite poor decision-making and rights violations.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau prosecutor investigates vicar's death
item.description: A special commission will spend 60 days investigating the killing of Vicar Luís Balanta.

item.title: Morocco wins Arab beach soccer cup for first time
item.description: The Moroccan national team defeated Mauritania 6-5 in a dramatic final match held in Port-Said, Egypt.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea education ministry seeks stronger school oversight
item.description: New director general aims to improve evaluation and supervision of national schools.

item.title: Mauritanian opposition denies rejecting UFP seat
item.description: The opposition coalition spokesperson stated that no decision has been made regarding the UFP's representation in the national dialogue commission.

item.title: Bonesha FM seeks 500 million francs to avoid closure
item.description: The independent radio station launched a 45-day fundraising campaign on Friday, October 30, to cover its financial shortfalls.

item.title: Tanzania scientists explore traditional medicine strategies
item.description: Government convenes practitioners, researchers, and investors to develop a national framework for local medicines.

item.title: Mauritania public projects incur 34 billion MRO in late penalties
item.description: 72 percent of 113 major public projects have exceeded deadlines, costing the state dearly.

item.title: Cameroon banks lend CFA5 billion to SMEs
item.description: AFG Bank and GBC will provide loans of up to CFA75 million with interest capped at 7.75% for women and youth entrepreneurs.

item.title: Burundian youth learns sewing after exam failure
item.description: Vanessa Munezero, from Muhanga, chose tailoring after failing state exams to start a new career.

item.title: Mauritanian navy joins Gulf of Guinea exercises
item.description: Naval forces from Mauritania participated in the annual 'Grand African NEMO 2026' drills from October 29 to November 6.

item.title: Kigali hosts Africa's Business Heroes summit
item.description: 10 entrepreneurs will pitch for $1.5 million in grant funding at the December 1-2 event.

item.title: Chad government backs off-season crops amid drought
item.description: Minister Keda Ballah announced support for producers facing a disrupted agricultural season due to irregular rains.

item.title: ANC vote share drops to 30.76% in 2026 local elections
item.description: The ruling party lost over 1.5 million votes compared to the 2021 municipal elections, facing coalition challenges.

item.title: Chapo launches 2026-27 agricultural campaign
item.description: President Daniel Chapo launched PROSPERA to connect producers with services, climate alerts, and markets.

item.title: Mauritania signs hajj agreement in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The deal covers the 1448 H pilgrimage season, with ministers from both nations meeting in Jeddah.

item.title: Tunisia proposes lower import taxes for solar equipment
item.description: The 2027 finance bill includes a 10% duty on solar sensors and tax exemptions for battery imports.

item.title: Fuel shortage sparks inflation in Bangui
item.description: Transport costs and food prices are rising as stations struggle with supply for three weeks.

item.title: Expert urges stronger fight against deforestation in DR Congo
item.description: An environmental expert in Muanda calls for increased action against tree felling due to heavy rains.

item.title: Vozinha wins Chilean league title with Colo-Colo
item.description: The Cape Verdean goalkeeper secured his team's 35th national title with a crucial late save.

item.title: Two officers interdicted over illegal Service Passport scheme
item.description: Ministry of Foreign Affairs refers Mahama Yahaya Amantana and Alhassan Sumani to police for investigation into alleged bribery.

item.title: Blaise Lasm trial delayed again
item.description: Ivory Coast court postpones hearing for detained PPA-CI official until November 16
